Further, the parties agree that should at any time the Florida law applicable to such evaluation procedures be changed or overturned by final order of a court of competent jurisdiction to which the Pinellas County School Board is subject, then in that event the parties agree to promptly renew collective bargaining negotiations for the purposes of modifying the procedures set forth in this article.

The evaluation forms and procedures to be used will comply with all requirements as set forth in Section 1012.34, F.S.

In accordance with Section 1012.34, F.S. teachers in their first three (3) years of employment will be rated as either Highly Effective, Effective, Developing or Unsatisfactory.

Pursuant to Florida law, a teacher on a probationary contract may be dismissed without cause, may be non-renewed without cause or may resign from the contractual position without breach of contract.

Derogatory material that has not been brought to the attention of the teacher pursuant to Florida Statute shall not be admissible in any action against the teacher.

School files are considered to be personnel files as defined in Florida Statutes.

Annual, PSC or CC teachers have the right to appeal their Final Evaluation if the rating would constitute grounds for termination pursuant to Section 1012.33, F.S. and Section 1012.335, F.S.

This panel’s decision is final but does not replace a right to a hearing under Section 1012.33, F.S. and Section 1012.335, F.S.

The Board may not award a probationary contract more than once to the same teacher except as provided under S. 1012.335 F.S..

Any teacher who held a professional service contract or continuing contract as of July 1, 2011, will continue to hold them in accordance with Sec. 1012.33 and this Agreement.

Those teachers who held professional service contracts or continuing contracts as of July 1, 2011, will continue to hold them in accordance with Sec. 1012.33 and this Agreement.

The district school superintendent, after receiving the recommendations required by Sec. 1012.34, charges the teacher with unsatisfactory performance and notifies the teacher of performance deficiencies as required by Sec. 1012.34;

The teacher receives two (2) consecutive annual performance evaluation ratings of unsatisfactory under s. 1012.34, two (2) annual performance evaluation ratings of unsatisfactory within a three (3) year period under s. 1012.34, or three consecutive annual performance evaluation ratings of needs improvement or a combination of needs improvement and unsatisfactory under Sec. 1012.34.

Hold an active professional certificate or temporary certificate issued pursuant to s. 1012.56 and rules of the State Board of Education;

based upon the individual’s evaluation under s. 1012.34 and approved by the Board; and

The teacher receives two (2) consecutive annual performance evaluation ratings of unsatisfactory under s. 1012.34, two (2) annual performance evaluation ratings of unsatisfactory within a three (3) year period under s. 1012.34, or three consecutive annual performance evaluation ratings of needs improvement or a combination of needs improvement and unsatisfactory under Sec. 1012.34.
